def is_palindrome(text: str) -> bool:
    """Return True when *text* reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring case
    and every character that is not a letter or a digit.
    """
    filtered = ''.join(ch.lower() for ch in text if ch.isalnum())
    return filtered == filtered[::-1]

def is_anagram(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
    """Return True when *a* and *b* contain the same letters with the same counts,
    ignoring case and every non-letter character.
    """
    # Filter out non-letter characters and convert to lowercase
    filtered_a = [ch.lower() for ch in a if ch.isalpha()]
    filtered_b = [ch.lower() for ch in b if ch.isalpha()]
    # Compare sorted lists of letters
    return sorted(filtered_a) == sorted(filtered_b)

def is_perfect_square(n: int) -> bool:
    """Return True when *n* is the square of a whole number. Negative numbers are never
    perfect squares.
    """

        return False
    root = math.isqrt(n)

def max_subarray_sum(numbers: list) -> int:
    """Return the largest sum of any non-empty contiguous slice of *numbers*. Raise
    ValueError for an empty list.
    """
    if not numbers:
        raise ValueError("Empty list")

    current_max = numbers[0]
    global_max = numbers[0]

    for num in numbers[1:]:
        current_max = max(num, current_max + num)
        global_max = max(global_max, current_max)

    return global_max

def insertion_sort(numbers: list) -> list:
    """Return a sorted copy of *numbers* using insertion sort. Do not call sorted() or
    .sort(), and do not modify the input.
    """
    sorted_list = list(numbers)
    for i in range(1, len(sorted_list)):
        key = sorted_list[i]
        j = i - 1
        while j >= 0 and sorted_list[j] > key:
            sorted_list[j + 1] = sorted_list[j]
            j -= 1
        sorted_list[j + 1] = key
    return sorted_list

def take(items: list, n: int) -> list:
    """Return the first *n* elements. A negative *n* gives an empty list, and an *n* larger
    than the list gives the whole list.
    """
    if n < 0:
        return []
    return items[:n]

def last_n(items: list, n: int) -> list:
    """Return the last *n* elements in their original order. A negative or zero *n* gives
    an empty list.
    """
    if n <= 0:
        return []
    return items[-n:]

def drop_none(items: list) -> list:
    """Remove every None from the list, keeping the order. Falsy values that are not None,
    such as 0 and '', are kept.
    """
    return [item for item in items if item is not None]

def split_or_empty(text: str, sep: str = ',') -> list:
    """Split *text* on *sep* and strip each part, dropping parts that are empty after
    stripping. An empty or whitespace-only input gives an empty list.
    """
    if sep == '':
        return []
    parts = text.split(sep)
    return [part.strip() for part in parts if part.strip()]

gotchas.text: Tool calling needs SGLang with the minicpm5 tool-call parser (sgl-project/sglang#25600). The openbmb cookbook says to install SGLang from main because v0.5.12.post1 lacked it; the PyPI 0.5.20 wheel used here ships it, so no source build is needed any more. The model writes XML tool calls (<function name="x"><param name="k">v</param></function>) and they come back as OpenAI tool_calls with finish_reason tool_calls, with thinking on and off.

SGLang has no MiniCPM5 reasoning parser, but the model uses plain <think> ... </think>, so --reasoning-parser qwen3 splits it into reasoning_content. With enable_thinking left unset the template adds no <think> prefix; the model opens the tag itself and the qwen3 parser still catches it.

flashinfer JIT-compiles its prefill kernels on the first request and shells out to ninja. In a venv that is not activated the first prefill dies with FileNotFoundError: ninja and the scheduler exits; put the venv bin directory on PATH before starting the server.
In a llama.cpp deployment the card warns that the default min_p 0.05 causes repetition and asks for min_p 0; the SGLang default min_p is already 0.
